cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven strip-cloth tobe/riga-style gown with white-on-white embroidery, a garment form widely worn across West African Sahelian peoples including the Wolof; nothing contradicts the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: gown; textile; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe, riga), hand-woven from hand-spun white/cream cotton. The body is formed of 82 narrow strips hand-sewn together along the selvedges vertically, while the sleeves are sewn horizontally. A large pocket is added at the front. The gown is hand-embroidered in white in the ‘two knives’ (aska biyu) pattern. The two knives and the area around the neck are embroidered with European thread onto a cotton base that has been couched down onto the tunic. Other areas are embroidered in cotton with chain and buttonhole eyelet stitching forming diamonds, squares and loops; there are large spirals on both the front and the back of the robe. The gown is unlined, and the sleeves of the garment are sewn with a hem; the neck and bottom are not.
